traces.title: German contact sector, Belgorod–Izyum, March 18, 1943
traces.note: Traced only along the inspected March 18 hachured line. The rest of the front is not completed by inference.

traces.title: German counterstroke towards Kharkov: schematic operation direction
traces.note: Source direction arrow, shown only after the complete captioned campaign interval; it does not trace a road or daily movement.

traces.title: German counterstroke against the advanced Soviet grouping in the Donbas
traces.note: Schematic source arrow around the exposed mobile grouping. Its entire campaign interval is the date range, not a reconstructed timetable.

traces.title: Approximate pre-Citadel contact, Orel–Kursk–Belgorod sectors, July 4, 1943
traces.note: The source legend dates this contact line July 4. On later selections it is an explicitly dated earlier comparison, not a claimed unchanged current front.

traces.title: Fourth and Ninth Army contact at the Hagen position, August 18, 1943
traces.note: Traced from the source’s separately keyed August 18 front. The line stops where this source trace ceases; no connecting front is invented.

traces.title: Northern limit of Citadel’s penetration, July 14, 1943
traces.note: Dotted source boundary records the farthest penetration, not an encirclement polygon or a control boundary. Displayed only on a later source-linked selection.

traces.title: German contact along the Dnieper and lower front, October 2, 1943
traces.note: Regional source contact, traced from the October 2 legend. River geography and front geometry remain distinct; no precise control shading is inferred.

traces.title: German contact after the Dnieper battles, December 21, 1943
traces.note: Separate December 21 source contact in the main map; the Kiev inset is not transformed by this registration and is not copied into this line.

traces.title: Army Group North contact before the offensive, January 14, 1944
traces.note: Source’s January 14 contact. No city, country or sovereignty boundary is inferred from its position.

traces.title: Army Group North contact at the Panther position, March 31, 1944
traces.note: The dashed March 31 line is source-dated separately from January 14. The southern endpoint stops at the inspected source segment; it is not extended across a gap.

traces.title: Crimean offensive: schematic advance from the northern isthmuses
traces.note: The source arrow summarises the captioned April 8–May 13 operation. Displayed only at the completed source-map endpoint; intermediate daily positions are not reconstructed.

traces.title: Crimean offensive: schematic advance from the Kerch Peninsula
traces.note: Generalised source arrow, not a verified unit route. The captioned campaign interval supplies the extent of the overview, not the departure day of every formation.

traces.title: Karelian Isthmus contact at the opening ground offensive, June 10, 1944
traces.note: Only the source’s June 10 contact segment on the Karelian Isthmus is traced. June 9 air/artillery preparation is not assigned this later ground-front geometry. Northern Karelia is outside this trace’s geographic control envelope.

traces.title: Contact from Ostrov towards Vitebsk, June 22, 1944
traces.note: Printed June 22 contact, northern segment. The source is a later U.S. Army reconstruction; this is not a contemporary surveyed line.

traces.title: Contact through the Orsha–Mogilev–Bobruisk sectors, June 22, 1944
traces.note: Printed June 22 contact only. Connecting vertices follow the drawn source line; no administrative or military-held-area polygon is derived.

traces.title: Contact from Dvinsk towards Vilnius, July 18, 1944
traces.note: Printed July 18 front, northern segment. It is not shown on June selections or as a supposed July 3 front.

traces.title: Contact through the Vilnius–Grodno approaches, July 18, 1944
traces.note: Source-dated pursuit endpoint. The line’s generalisation does not settle local resistance, the security of every road, or political authority.

traces.title: Contact north of Brest, July 18, 1944
traces.note: Southern continuation of the July 18 source front, shown as regional context only. No later July offensive is imported from other source sheets.

traces.title: Earlier source label: Fourth Panzer Army
traces.note: The dashed German army box appears on the Dnieper approaches. A formation label describes an operational grouping, not a headquarters building. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: Popov mobile group
traces.note: The Soviet group is labelled "POPOV" inside the southern counteroffensive area. Its printed position is a regional source-map reference. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: First Panzer Army
traces.note: The German army label lies by the Donbas sector and the counterstroke arrows. The arrowed area represents the operation over its stated interval. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: German Ninth Army
traces.note: The NINTH label sits at the northern face of the Kursk salient, below the Orel sector. Labels locate army sectors at this regional scale. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: Steppe reserve grouping
traces.note: The dashed reserve area prints the Twenty-Seventh, Fifty-Third and Fifth Guards formations. A reserve grouping is distinct from the first assault line. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: SS Panzer corps sector
traces.note: The German SS Pz label appears in the southern attack area. The regional sheet does not resolve individual tank positions around Prokhorovka. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: Second Guards Army
traces.note: The solid-outline Soviet Second Guards Army box stands at the northern approaches to Perekop. It identifies a source-map operational sector. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: Fifty-first Army
traces.note: The source labels the Soviet Fifty-first Army at the northern Crimean approaches, separate from Second Guards Army. The label is not a headquarters address. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

traces.title: Earlier source label: German Seventeenth Army
traces.note: The broken-outline Seventeenth Army box identifies the German command on the peninsula. It does not show the exact perimeter occupied by every subordinate unit. This point georeferences the printed sector label, not a current deployment, headquarters or unit footprint. Its caption interval does not prove unchanged occupation of this point. The selected date is later than the source interval.

limitations: Later U.S. Army reconstruction, not contemporary unit plotting.
Registration fit does not measure battlefield accuracy.

No interpolation, control polygons, unverified per-day formation positions or exact unit routes. Nine source-label sector references are shown only after their captioned intervals, as earlier comparisons.
